name: Starter: German
about: German in real, everyday sentences, with each one's words in German order.

words.Haus: house; zu Hause: at home; von zu Hause: from home; nach Hause: home
words.hin: there (direction toward a destination, away from the speaker)
words.freuen: to please; freut mich: nice to meet you
words.gern: gladly; with a verb: like to
words.geben: to give; es gibt: there is, there are
words.fahren: to go (by car, train or bike); to drive

freut-mich.about: Literally pleases me: what you say when you meet someone.

ich-moechte.about: The polite way to ask for something: Ich möchte einen Kaffee.

concept.line: Most verbs end in -e with ich, -st with du, -t with er, sie, es or ihr, and -en with wir, sie or Sie; if the part before -en ends in s, ß, x or z, du takes only -t: ich arbeite, du arbeitest, wir arbeiten, du heißt.
In a main clause the verb comes second.
Every noun is masculine (der), feminine (die) or neuter (das), and ein, kein, mein and the rest match it: der Bahnhof, die Bank, das Haus.
In a yes-or-no question the verb comes first; after a question word, it comes next: Wo wohnst du (where live you).
When a masculine noun is the object of the verb, der becomes den and ein becomes einen: Ich habe den Zug verpasst (I have the train missed).

words.means: wohne = live; wohnst = live; wohnt = lives
there (direction toward a destination, away from the speaker)

concept.line: Use nach with cities and most countries, zu with people and places such as work, and in with places you go into: nach München, zur Arbeit, ins Kino.
